lines.text: The old lift operator gave me one rule on my first day.
After closing, if a chair comes down the mountain with someone in it... don't help them off. Let it go around.
My first night alone, the snow fell so thick I couldn't see the top towers.
At nine, I shut the lift down. The empty chairs swayed to a stop, creaking in the wind.
Then, somewhere up in the dark, the cable started to hum.
One chair was coming down. Slowly. With the motor off.
Someone was sitting in it. Bar down. Head bowed. Covered in snow.
It stopped right in front of me... and waited.
I didn't move. I didn't speak. I kept my hands in my pockets.
After a long time, the cable groaned... and carried it back up into the snow.
I grabbed the radio and called the top hut. Did someone just ride down?
Nobody up here, kid. But a chair just came over the top... and it's empty.
Then I turned around. A line of fresh footprints crossed the snow... right into my little hut. And none came back out.
